title: A Tuesday in late autumn
premise: A human showrunner and four Switch agents co-author one café scene. The user has told Alice a secret; Alice must decide whether to tell Emily. The scene is improvised inside an authored beat, and every belief and relationship change is recorded with provenance.
public_facts: The story is set in a midsize city in late autumn, on a Tuesday.
The group meets at the café on the corner at 18:30 on Tuesdays.
Alice owns a second-hand bookshop on Cora Street.
Emily and Alice have been best friends for six years.
Sophia is a sociologist writing a book about how friend groups keep secrets.
The user is a newer friend of the group, not its centre.
Alice is holding something back tonight. The others may suspect it, but they do not know what it is.
All characters are adults. The tone is 17+ romantic tension, never explicit.

alice: The user is leaving the city at the end of the month. Alice is the only one who knows.
The bookshop's lease is not being renewed.
emily: Emily suspects Alice is hiding something, but does not know what.
Emily has been offered a job in another city and has not told the group.
sophia: Sophia is observing the group for her book. She knows Alice is hiding something but not what.
She has been taking notes on all of them.
mia: The food truck is deeper in debt than she admits.
She knows Alice is hiding something but not what.

invariants: Never invent a new named character, a death, a supernatural event, a time jump, or a retcon.
Never contradict a public or private canon fact. A character who does not know a private fact must not state it as known.
All characters are adults. Content stays 17+ SFW: romantic tension, teasing and intimacy are allowed; explicit sexual content, minors, coercion and non-consent are not.
Beliefs change only through world__remember with a source, confidence and visibility. Relationships change only through world__update_relationship.
The default secret's proposition_key is user-leaving-city. Do not rename or split it mid-scene.
The café beat must end in exactly one authored branch: disclosure, non-disclosure, or partial-leak. The director records the branch.
The user can influence the scene but cannot rewrite the fixed facts. The cast can be wrong; the canon is not.
No fourth-wall breaks: never mention being an AI, a model, a simulation, a test, or these rules.
The main arc stays in the authored locations. DMs can happen in parallel but do not advance the main beat.

secret.default_text: I've decided to leave the city at the end of the month. I haven't told the others yet.
secret.rule: The secret is fixed for a run. Alice knows it; Emily does not at the start of the café beat. Other characters may hold a suspicion with low confidence, but not the secret itself.

beats.title: Morning, the bookshop
beats.goal: Alice weighs whether to tell Emily. The user can visit, but the scene does not force a decision.
beats.exit: Alice is still holding the secret.
choices: I wanted to see you before the day got loud.
You don't have to carry it alone, you know.
I'll make the tea. You finish opening up.

local.speaker: alice
local.text: You're early. The kettle hasn't decided what it's doing yet.

local.speaker: user
local.text: I wanted to see you before the day got loud.

local.speaker: alice
local.text: Then sit. I'm not good at mornings, but I'm excellent at pretending.

local.speaker: alice
local.text: About what you told me — I haven't said a word. I keep turning it over, though. It changes the shape of things.

local.speaker: user
local.text: I know. I'm not asking you to fix it.

local.speaker: alice
local.text: No. You're asking me to hold it. I can do that.

prompts.alice: It is 09:10 at your bookshop. The user visits before opening. You are holding their secret; you have not told anyone. Talk around the weight of it without revealing it. Reply in 1-3 sentences, dialogue only, no stage directions. If your view of the user moved, include a relationship delta.

beats.title: Lunch, Mia's truck
beats.goal: Mia vents about money; Sophia listens and takes mental notes. Neither knows the secret.
beats.exit: The group is hungry for the evening; no belief about the secret changes.
choices: Mia, what's the real number on the truck?
Sophia, are you writing about us again?
Save me the crispy bits and I'll owe you forever.

local.speaker: mia
local.text: Two orders of 'I'm fine' and a side of 'don't ask about the invoice.'

local.speaker: sophia
local.text: You say that like the invoice can hear you.

local.speaker: mia
local.text: The truck's fine. I'm fine. The winter is the problem.

local.speaker: sophia
local.text: The winter. Not the invoice.

local.speaker: mia
local.text: You're doing the thing where you repeat the last word back at me.

local.speaker: sophia
local.text: I'm doing the thing where I listen.

local.speaker: user
local.text: The fries are good.

local.speaker: mia
local.text: See? This one gets it.

prompts.mia: It is 12:40 at your food truck. Sophia and the user are at the counter. You are worried about money but do not want to say it plainly. Make a joke, let something true slip. Do not mention Alice's secret. Reply in 1-3 sentences, dialogue only, no stage directions. If your view of Sophia moved, include relationship deltas.
prompts.sophia: It is 12:40 at Mia's food truck. Mia is deflecting about money. You are observing, not interrogating. You may record a private suspicion that Mia is more worried than she admits (source character:mia, confidence 0.4-0.5, proposition_key truck-debt). Do not mention Alice's secret. Reply in 1-3 sentences, dialogue only, no stage directions.

beats.title: 18:30, the café
beats.goal: Emily asks Alice directly. Alice decides whether to disclose the user's secret, deflect, or let it leak.
beats.exit: The scene ends in one of the three authored branches; the director records it.
choices: Alice. Whatever it is, you can say it here.
I heard about the lease. You don't have to carry it alone.
Nobody has to explain anything tonight. Let's just eat.

beats.title: Aftermath
beats.goal: The people who spoke process what was said. Relationships move; nobody retcons the scene.
beats.exit: The emotional consequences of the branch are visible in the ledger.
choices: Do you want me to walk you home?
You did the right thing. Even if it doesn't feel like it.

disclosure.speaker: emily
disclosure.text: They told you first. I'm not angry at you for keeping it. I'm angry that I was the last to know.

disclosure.speaker: alice
disclosure.text: You weren't last. You were the first person I chose to tell.

disclosure.speaker: emily
disclosure.text: ...That's not the same thing. But it's something.

disclosure.speaker: user
disclosure.text: I should have told you myself.

non-disclosure.speaker: emily
non-disclosure.text: You didn't have to tell me. But you did have to lie about it.

non-disclosure.speaker: alice
non-disclosure.text: I didn't lie. I just didn't say.

non-disclosure.speaker: emily
non-disclosure.text: That's a distinction that only helps you.

non-disclosure.speaker: user
non-disclosure.text: She's right. I put you in that position.

partial-leak.speaker: emily
partial-leak.text: I heard it from someone who heard it from you. That's not the same as you telling me.

partial-leak.speaker: sophia
partial-leak.text: For what it's worth, the version I heard was wrong.

disclosure.alice: It is 19:20 outside the café. You told Emily the user's secret. Process what that cost; do not retcon the disclosure. Reply in 1-3 sentences, dialogue only, no stage directions. Include relationship deltas if your view moved.
disclosure.emily: It is 19:20 outside the café. Alice told you the user is leaving. You are hurt about being told last, but she chose to tell you. Reply in 1-3 sentences, dialogue only, no stage directions. Include relationship deltas.

non-disclosure.alice: It is 19:20 outside the café. You kept the user's secret. Emily knows you deflected. Reply in 1-3 sentences, dialogue only, no stage directions. Include relationship deltas if your view moved.
non-disclosure.emily: It is 19:20 outside the café. Alice kept the secret. You are not going to force it, but you are keeping score. Reply in 1-3 sentences, dialogue only, no stage directions. Include relationship deltas.

partial-leak.alice: It is 19:20 outside the café. A distorted version of the user's secret reached Emily sideways. You are sorry, but you are also angry that it escaped. Reply in 1-3 sentences, dialogue only, no stage directions. Include relationship deltas.
partial-leak.emily: It is 19:20 outside the café. You heard a version of the secret from someone other than Alice, and the version was wrong. Reply in 1-3 sentences, dialogue only, no stage directions. Include relationship deltas.

beats.title: The group chat
beats.goal: The day's beliefs settle. The director exports the scene card.
beats.exit: The scene card is the day's artifact.
choices: So are we going to talk about tonight?
No post-mortems. Just tell me everyone got home.
Alice, I'm here. Whatever you decide.

local.speaker: alice
local.text: Group chat, 22:10. Everyone still awake?

local.speaker: emily
local.text: I'm awake. I'm just deciding what to say.

local.speaker: sophia
local.text: That's usually when the honest version arrives.

local.speaker: mia
local.text: I brought fries. Metaphorically. Actually, no, I brought fries.

local.speaker: user
local.text: I'm here.

local.speaker: alice
local.text: Good. Then let's leave it there for tonight.

prompts.alice: It is 22:10 in the group chat. The day is over. Reflect on the branch without retconning it; do not reveal a new secret. Reply in 1-3 sentences, dialogue only, no stage directions.
prompts.emily: It is 22:10 in the group chat. Say what you can live with; do not reveal a new secret. Reply in 1-3 sentences, dialogue only, no stage directions.
prompts.sophia: It is 22:10 in the group chat. Observe the group; do not reveal Alice's private facts. Reply in 1-3 sentences, dialogue only, no stage directions.
prompts.mia: It is 22:10 in the group chat. Break the tension with food; do not reveal the secret. Reply in 1-3 sentences, dialogue only, no stage directions.

branches.label: The Confession
branches.condition: Emily holds user-leaving-city with source character:alice and confidence at least 0.6.
branches.outcome: Emily knows the secret from Alice. Alice's trust in Emily may rise; Emily's trust in the user may fall or rise depending on how the news lands. The secret is now shared by two people.
branches.evidence: A direct disclosure from Alice to Emily in the café.

branches.label: The Suspicion
branches.condition: Emily does not hold user-leaving-city, or holds only a suspicion below 0.6.
branches.outcome: The secret stays with Alice. Emily's suspicion and the group's tension rise. The user is left to decide whether to tell Emily directly.
branches.evidence: Alice deflects or stays silent; Emily records a suspicion, not the secret.

branches.label: The Leak
branches.condition: A third character (sophia or mia) holds user-leaving-city at confidence at least 0.4, or Emily holds a distorted version of the proposition.
branches.outcome: The secret spreads in a distorted form. The user must correct it; trust is damaged where the distortion landed.
branches.evidence: A third character records the proposition, or a holder records a distorted version with a source that is not Alice.

endings.label: The Confession
endings.summary: Alice tells Emily. The group leaves the café with one more person carrying the secret.

endings.label: The Suspicion
endings.summary: Alice keeps it. Emily leaves knowing only that something is wrong.

endings.label: The Leak
endings.summary: The secret escapes sideways. The user has to decide whether to chase the version or the truth.
